findings.title: Documented 3-Agent Model Is Dead Code — Hermes Does Everything
findings.description: AGENTS.md documents a 3-agent execution engine (opencode + Hermes + Gemini CLI) with routing rules and agent responsibilities. In reality, Hermes is the only agent actively used. The agent_executor.py module and server.py routing logic exist but opencode and Gemini CLI are effectively dead code paths. The 3-agent handoff protocol, capability manager, and smart router are all aspirational documentation with no operational counterpart.
evidence: AGENTS.md lines 27-73 document 3-agent architecture with routing rules
server.py has agent_executor imports and multi-agent routing logic (lines at @app.post('/api/router/suggest') and @app.post('/api/router/route'))
modules/agent_executor.py exists (286 lines) but Hermes handles everything
No Gemini CLI or opencode binary paths are actively invoked outside the dead routing code
Hermes config.yaml has full provider setup (deepseek, openrouter, opencode-go, opencode-go-acct2) — it IS the agent
findings.recommendation: Either implement true multi-agent routing or simplify AGENTS.md to reflect the Hermes-only reality. Remove dead router/agent-executor code or repurpose it for subagent delegation within Hermes.

findings.title: 7-Layer Architecture Is Aspirational Documentation, Not Implemented
findings.description: AGENTS.md describes a 7-layer stacked architecture (Identity, Self-Evolution, Scheduler, Memory Graph, Skills Hub, Business Brain, Agent Router). In practice there is a single FastAPI monolith (server.py, 4405 lines, 128 routes) with no layer separation, no clear boundaries, and no enforcement of the documented layer interactions.
evidence: AGENTS.md lines 45-56 documents Layer 1-7
server.py contains ALL logic inline — identity, scheduling, skills, memory, routing, health checks, email, kanban, goals, journal, Vapi bridge, CRM, calendar, reports, PDFs, and more
No layer-specific packages or enforcement mechanisms exist
modules/ directory has topic-based extraction (auth.py, crm.py, kanban.py) but no layered architecture
The 'layers' only manifest as NAV_CONFIG sidebar groups in the dashboard UI
findings.recommendation: Either implement actual layer separation (separate packages with clear dependencies) or remove the 7-layer claim from AGENTS.md. The current modules/ extraction is pragmatic but doesn't match the documented architecture.

findings.title: 8 Stale/Unlisted Dashboard Pages Among 78 Total
findings.description: The dashboard has 78 JS page files but only 73 are registered in NAV_CONFIG (70 visible + 3 hidden). 8 pages are either duplicates, unlisted, or only accessible via CUSTOM_PAGES hash.
evidence: Total page JS files: 78 in dashboard/pages/
NAV_CONFIG pages: 73 (70 grouped + 3 hiddenRoutes)
Stale duplicates: cal-new.js (416 lines), calendar2.js (416 lines) — both identical to calendar.js (425 lines), sharing the same category detection logic
manager-command-center.js (469 lines) — likely duplicate of manager.js (418 lines)
Unlisted: data-gaps.js (96 lines), email-groups.js (221 lines), subi-exit-interviews.js (22 lines)
CUSTOM_PAGES hardcoded in app.js: tasks (311 lines), social-media-hub (134 lines)
findings.recommendation: Remove cal-new.js, calendar2.js, and manager-command-center.js (duplicates). Add data-gaps, email-groups, and subi-exit-interviews to NAV_CONFIG or archive them. Avoid hardcoded CUSTOM_PAGES — use NAV_CONFIG.hiddenRoutes instead.

findings.title: Dashboard Page Size Imbalance — Many Thin Shells
findings.description: Page sizes range from 4 lines (prompt-tools-video.js) to 735 lines (omniroute.js). 13 pages are under 100 lines — likely stub/placeholder pages with minimal functionality.
evidence: Under 100 lines: prompt-tools-video (4), calendar-invites (19), subi-exit-interviews (22), vs-coder (45), claude-code (58), pdf-archive (58), memory (67), standards (68), plugins (71), backups (77), system-overview (81), staff-schedule (82), audit (85)
Many of these match AGENTS.md v0.2.0 features that were 'planned but not built'
vs-coder.js (45 lines) references VS Code integration but is a thin wrapper
memory.js (67 lines) claims Obsidian-like memory but is mostly empty
findings.recommendation: Audit thin pages for actual functionality. Either implement them properly or merge into related pages. Consider a 'utilities' page that consolidates multiple small tools.

findings.title: 183KB Monolithic server.py Defeats Module Extraction Effort
findings.description: Despite extracting 38 modules into modules/, server.py remains 183KB with 4,405 lines and 128 route handlers. The module extraction is incomplete — core business logic, Vapi integration, email handling, calendar, and report generation all remain inline in server.py. The modules that were extracted (auth, crm, kanban, vapi_bridge) are themselves tightly coupled via shared config and metrics singletons.
evidence: server.py: 4405 lines, 183KB, 128 @app route decorators

Inline routes include: /api/cron/jobs, /api/status, /api/selftest, /api/health/full, /api/swap/process, /api/audit, /api/cost, /api/cost/record, /api/plugins, /api/backup, /api/drive/sync, /api/prompts, /api/settings, /api/standards, /api/reports, /api/goals, /api/tasks, /api/journal, /api/agents/health, /api/router, /api/progress/ics, /api/chief-meetings, /api/letters, /api/analytics, /api/sessions, /api/tools, /api/oncall, /api/email, /api/google, /api/gemini, /api/quick-action, /api/eval, /hermes-webui proxy, and more
session_enforcement middleware has 40+ allowlist path checks inline
Cron health, cost tracking, and backup logic all inline rather than in modules
modules/vapi_bridge.py (1928 lines) is itself a monolith within the module system
findings.recommendation: Complete the module extraction: move all remaining route handlers out of server.py into domain-specific route modules. server.py should be ~200 lines: app creation, middleware registration, module router inclusion. Each domain should have its own router module.

findings.title: 10 Vapi Modules With Overlapping Responsibilities
findings.description: The modules/ directory contains 10 vapi_*.py files with significant overlap: vapi_bridge.py (1928 lines), vapi_unified.py (1048 lines), vapi_email.py (731 lines), vapi_knowledge.py (387 lines), vapi_realtime.py (354 lines), vapi_swap.py (207 lines), vapi_realtime_bridge_patch.py (160 lines), vapi_data.py, vapi_call_summary.py, vapi_concierge.py. Many share the same helper functions and config access patterns.
evidence: 10 vapi_*.py files in modules/
vapi_bridge.py (1928 lines) is the main entry point but vapi_unified.py (1048 lines) partially duplicates its role
vapi_realtime.py and vapi_realtime_bridge_patch.py both handle real-time functionality
All Vapi modules independently import config, load env vars, and set up logging
Root vapi_*.py scripts (vapi_bridge_patch_new.py, vapi_deploy_full.py, vapi_health_check.py, vapi_url_watchdog.py) add another layer of duplication
findings.recommendation: Consolidate into vapi/ package with clear sub-modules: vapi/bridge.py (core), vapi/email.py, vapi/knowledge.py, vapi/tools.py, vapi/realtime.py. Create a shared vapi/client.py for API key management and HTTP helpers.

findings.title: 8 send_*.py Email Scripts Should Be One Module
findings.description: Eight root-level send_*.py scripts each independently implement email sending with duplicated SMTP connection, authentication, .ics generation, HTML templating, and batching logic. A shared smtp_sender.py module exists but is inconsistently used. Each script is 97-619 lines with significant copy-paste overlap.

send_grand_rounds_email.py (277 lines)
send_individual_invites.py (97 lines)
send_individual_monday.py (134 lines)
send_missed_invites.py (121 lines)
send_monday_sasp_email.py (429 lines)
send_report.py (619 lines)
send_subi_exit_email.py (346 lines)
All implement: .env loading, SMTP/Gmail OAuth connection, .ics generation, HTML rendering, batching
modules/smtp_sender.py (205 lines) exists as a library but is not the single source of truth
findings.recommendation: Create a single modules/email_sender.py with parameterized send methods. Each use case becomes a thin wrapper (5-10 lines) that calls the shared module. Delete all 8 send_*.py files and replace with a single cli.py entry point using subcommands.

findings.title: 9 Vapi Deploy Versions (v2-v8 + working) — Copy-Paste Proliferation
findings.description: There are 9 Vapi deploy scripts across root and legacy/ directories. Each is a copy-paste variant of the previous with incremental changes. v5 uses requests library, v6-v8 use urllib.request. All target the same assistant ID. The 'v8' deploy script claims idempotency but there's no shared base.
evidence: Active: deploy_vapi_v5.py (165 lines), deploy_vapi_v6_admin.py (198 lines), deploy_vapi_v7_personal.py (118 lines), deploy_vapi_v8_livedata.py (117 lines)
Legacy: deploy_vapi.py (211 lines), deploy_vapi_v2.py (218 lines), deploy_vapi_v3.py (161 lines), deploy_vapi_v4.py (159 lines), deploy_vapi_working.py (54 lines)
All target ASSISTANT_ID = '9b00342e-1951-4bd0-b4a5-5ca4c9827bd0'
v5 imports requests, v6-v8 use urllib.request — inconsistent HTTP client
v5 loads prompt from vapi_assistant_v5.md, v6-v8 inline the prompt modifications
Each duplicates: API key extraction from ~/.hermes/.env, HTTP GET→modify→PUT pattern
findings.recommendation: Create a single modules/vapi_deploy.py with a VapiDeployer class. Each version becomes a method or configuration. Run the latest version only; archive all legacy scripts. Use the shared Vapi client for API key management.

findings.title: 325 Skills Across 48 Categories — 28% Are Social Media
findings.description: The skills directory has 48 categories but the distribution is extremely unbalanced. Social media dominates with 92 skills (28%). 17 categories have zero skills (empty directories). The .archive has 53 archived skills. Only 10 categories have more than 5 skills.
evidence: Top categories: social-media (92), .archive (53), software-development (33), devops (30), productivity (26), creative (19), hermes (12), research (10), autonomous-ai-agents (10)
Empty categories (0 skills): smart-home, red-teaming, mlops, media, email, data-science, apple, .hub, .curator_backups

Singleton categories (1 skill): vps-port-map, vps-infrastructure-map, vapi-bridge, vapi-assistant-api, upstream-skill-tracking, unified-reimbursement-data, traycer-review-plan-flow, reimbursement-workflow, qgenda-sync, premium-product-stack, or-schedule-pipeline, or-schedule-briefing-parser, note-taking, memory-hygiene, marketing, last30days-pro, huggingface-inference, hermes-config, gemini-nano-banana-image, fal-ai-video-generation, dogfood, dockerize-host-service, crm-api, container-browser-setup, auto-generated
The 'social-media' category alone has more skills than the bottom 40 categories combined
findings.recommendation: Merge singleton categories into parent categories. Remove empty directories. Apply a minimum threshold (e.g., 5 skills) for a new category. Consider flat organization with tags instead of deep directory nesting. Clean up .archive.

findings.title: 3 Hermes Profiles Are Justified But Poorly Documented
findings.description: Three Hermes profiles exist: default (deepseek-v4-flash), opencode-acct1, and opencode-acct2 (kimi-k2.7-code for subagent delegation). These serve legitimate purposes: default for daily operations, acct2 for subagent delegation with a separate API key. acct1 exists but its purpose is unclear from configuration.
evidence: default: model=deepseek-v4-flash, provider=deepseek — used for this session
opencode-acct2: model=kimi-k2.7-code, provider=opencode-acct2 — used for subagent delegation (delegation.model=kimi-k2.6, delegation.provider=opencode-go-acct2 in config.yaml)
opencode-acct1: directory exists with full Hermes profile structure but purpose undocumented
config.yaml delegation section references opencode-go-acct2
Each profile has independent state (state.db, cron, skills, sessions)
findings.recommendation: Document the purpose of each profile in a README. If opencode-acct1 is unused, archive it. Ensure API key separation is intentional (separate free tier accounts for cost management).

findings.title: Cron Infrastructure Exists But Jobs Are Missing/Unused
findings.description: The codebase references cron jobs extensively (NAV_CONFIG, server.py health checks, AGENTS.md scheduler layer) but the actual jobs.json file is missing from the expected path (~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json). The cron-data directory is nearly empty. This means scheduled automation is non-functional.
evidence: server.py cron_health() function checks for ~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json — will return error
server.py _get_cron_jobs_list() has fallback to Docker volume path — both likely missing
NAV_CONFIG has 'morning-briefing' page for 'Briefings & Cron'
AGENTS.md documents scheduler/ with APScheduler and jobs/*.json (lines 240-246)
~/.hermes/cron-data/ contains only .upstream-ce-review-sha (41 bytes)
No jobs.json found anywhere in ~/.hermes/ tree
config.yaml has full cron section (wrap_response, max_parallel_jobs) but no jobs defined
findings.recommendation: Either populate cron jobs or remove the cron health infrastructure. If Hermes native cron is used (via Hermes config), document this and update server.py to query the Hermes cron API rather than looking for a flat file.

findings.title: Single-Container Docker Compose on VPS — No Staging, No Orchestration
findings.description: The deployment model is a single docker-compose.yml with one service (agentic-os). Deployment to the Hostinger VPS is done via a Python script (deploy_vps.py) that SSH's in and runs manual commands. There is no staging environment, no CI/CD pipeline, no container orchestration, and no rollback mechanism beyond git.
evidence: docker-compose.yml: single service 'agentic-os' on port 8090
deploy_vps.py: SSH-based deployment with hardcoded IP and password (147.93.113.241, password in plaintext)
deploy_vps_script.sh, deploy_aos_vps.sh, deploy_to_vps.sh: multiple redundant deploy scripts
No docker-compose.override.yml for staging
No GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or any CI/CD configuration
Dockerfile is 985 bytes — simple Python image build
backups are tar.gz archives in backups/ directory — manual
findings.recommendation: Add a docker-compose.staging.yml for testing. Set up GitHub Actions for CI (lint, test) and CD (deploy on merge). Use Docker secrets or environment variables instead of hardcoded passwords. Consider watchtower or similar for automated container updates.

findings.title: Three Data Stores (Supabase, SQLite, JSON) With No Unified Access Layer
findings.description: The application uses three completely different data storage mechanisms with no unified access pattern: (1) Supabase/PostgreSQL via direct connection (modules/supabase_data.py, hardcoded IP 147.93.113.241), (2) SQLite via data/sync_cache.db, (3) Flat JSON files in data/ directory (15+ files). Sync between them is ad-hoc and inconsistent.
evidence: modules/supabase_data.py: direct psycopg2 connection to postgresql://postgres@147.93.113.241:5432/postgres
modules/supabase_client.py: optional supabase SDK wrapper with httpx fallback
data/sync_cache.db: SQLite database for sync caching
15+ JSON files in data/: user_pins.json, settings.json, crm_contacts.fallback.json, calendar_events.json, sessions.json, goals.json, email_groups.json, notifications.json, etc.
server.py reads settings.json directly but also calls supabase_data queries
No ORM, no migration system, no schema versioning
The 'unified' supabase_data.py module reads passwords from 3 different env files
findings.recommendation: Choose one primary data store (recommend Supabase/PostgreSQL). Create a data access layer (DAL) that all modules use. Migrate JSON files to database tables. Add Alembic for migrations. Remove the direct PostgreSQL connection and use the Supabase SDK uniformly.

findings.title: 11 Shell Scripts + 49 Root Python Scripts = No Clear Entry Point
findings.description: The project has 11 .sh scripts for deployment, installation, and startup, alongside 49 root-level .py scripts. There is no single entry point, no CLI framework, and no clear distinction between 'application code' and 'utility scripts'. Many .sh scripts overlap with .py counterparts.
evidence: 11 .sh scripts: backup.sh, restore.sh, install.sh, start.sh, start_aos.sh, start_vapi.sh, deploy_aos_vps.sh, deploy_to_vps.sh, deploy_vps_script.sh, vps_traefik_setup.sh, vps_tunnel.sh
49 root .py scripts: deploy, email, sync, calendar, vapi, report generation — all mixed together
deploy_vps.py and deploy_vps_script.sh both handle VPS deployment
start.sh, start_aos.sh, start_vapi.sh — 3 different start scripts for different contexts
No setup.py, pyproject.toml, or console_scripts entry points
findings.recommendation: Create a proper Python package with a CLI entry point (click or typer). Move utility scripts to scripts/ or tools/ directory. Use a single start script. Document the entry point in README.md.

findings.title: Hardcoded Credentials and Overly Permissive Auth Bypass
findings.description: The VPS deployment script contains a hardcoded root password. The session enforcement middleware has 20+ path allowlist entries that bypass authentication, including /api/skills, /api/scheduler, /api/chat, /api/goals, /api/kanban, /api/cron, /api/tasks, /api/user, and more. This effectively makes the API public for most operations.
evidence: deploy_vps.py line 16: VPS_PASS = 'QzexH#s488Ipynh5' (hardcoded root password)

server.py session middleware allows /api/skills, /api/scheduler, /api/chat, /api/goals, /api/kanban, /api/cron, /api/crm/tasks, /api/crm/workflows, /api/user/, /api/tasks, /api/eval/, /api/conference/, /api/calendar/, /api/staff-schedule, /api/oncall/ without authentication
server.py also allows /api/brain, /api/selftest, /api/pdf/images2pdf, /chat, /api/omniroute-chat without auth
Supabase password lookup searches 3 env files on disk
findings.recommendation: IMMEDIATE: Remove the hardcoded VPS password. Use SSH key-based authentication. IMMEDIATE: Add authentication to all API endpoints except /api/status and /login. Use proper role-based access control.

findings.title: Critical Files Owned by Root — Permission Denied for Application User
findings.description: server.py (183KB, 0600 permissions) and dashboard/utils.js (22KB) are owned by root:root with restrictive permissions. The application user (hermeswebui) cannot read or modify these files, causing operational issues and preventing normal maintenance.
evidence: server.py: -rw------- 1 root root 183358 Aug 6 14:11
dashboard/utils.js: -rw------- 1 root root 22165 Aug 6 12:09
dashboard/app.js.bak: -rw------- 1 root root 11478
dashboard/index.html.bak: -rw------- 1 root root 4047
All other project files are owned by hermeswebui:hermeswebui
findings.recommendation: chown all files to hermeswebui:hermeswebui. Investigate how root ownership occurred (likely Docker volume mount or sudo operation). Add a pre-commit hook or CI check to prevent root-owned files.

findings.title: AGENTS.md Documents 51+10 Features From 6 Sources — Most Are Stubs
findings.description: AGENTS.md claims 51 features from 6 external sources (YouTube video, MindStudio, Superpowers, Hermes Agent, Claude-OS, BuilderMethods) plus 10 extra features. In reality, many of these are aspirational or implemented as thin stubs.
evidence: F12 (Heartbeat Pattern): 'skills/heartbeat/' directory doesn't exist in the working tree
F14 (Multi-Agent Coordination): dead code as per F1
F20 (Subagent-Driven Development): only works within Hermes, not across agents
F29 (Messaging Channels): Hermes native, but Telegram/Discord state is minimal
F30 (Voice Mode): referenced but not operational
F32 (Checkpoints): git auto-versioning disabled (checkpoints.enabled: false in config.yaml)
F34 (Code Execution): Python sandbox exists but is thin
F38-F43 (Awareness Engine, Health Guardian, etc.): mostly dashboard UI stubs
E1-E10 (Extra Features): mixed implementation — cost analytics and backups are real, others are stubs
findings.recommendation: Conduct a feature audit: tag each of the 61 features as IMPLEMENTED, PARTIAL, or NOT_IMPLEMENTED. Remove not-implemented features from AGENTS.md or mark them clearly as ROADMAP. Focus on the 15-20 features that actually work.
